messages:
Ava: Quick design q — customers asking for exports that show not just an event, but a human-readable change diff (who changed routing policy X from A -> B, with before/after config). How much extra do we need to store to emit that?
Marco: We already persist the full immutable event blob for each write op. Generating a diff on export is mostly a transformation, except for big configs where diffing can be expensive.
Priya: Agree. The tricky bit is identity + context: who made the change (service account vs user), request metadata (IP, region), and the previous snapshot id. We need hooks that tie events to the resource snapshots.
Jon: Two UX asks from compliance teams: 1) line-level diffs in the exported file (NDJSON with fields old/new) and 2) a preview in Console that highlights changed keys.
Ava: Console preview would be huge. We should also ensure export formats support both a compact diff and a full-blob fallback. e.g., ndjson: {event, actor, diff? or full_before, full_after}.
Marco: Proposal: default export includes event metadata + a concise structural diff if the changed object is < 10KB. For >10KB we include a URL to fetch the full before/after blobs (signed, short TTL) to avoid huge export files.
Priya: We also need retention controls. Some customers want 7y exports for audits. We can't keep full blobs forever in hot storage. Suggest lifecycle: 90d hot, 2y cold, snapshot export for long term.
Ava: @Marco can you estimate cost/latency impact of computing diffs on-the-fly vs storing precomputed diffs?
Marco: On-the-fly for small objects is cheap. For large objects or high-rate streams it's CPU intensive. Precomputing diffs at write time adds storage cost ~10-20% but makes exports fast. I lean precompute for any write that touches route/policy tables.
Jon: Also need RBAC on export endpoints. The export should only return events allowed by the caller's scope — customers often want service-level filtering and role-based redaction.
Priya: Redaction rules: PII may appear in some config fields (comments, secrets shouldn't be in config, but still). We should apply per-customer redaction policy with allowlists. Export schema should include a 'redaction_applied' flag and reason.
Ava: Example CLI export payload mockup for compliance team, thoughts?
Ava: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/audit/exports \
  -d '{"since":"2025-10-01T00:00:00Z","until":"2025-10-31T23:59:59Z","format":"ndjson","include_diffs":true,"max_object_size":10240,"filters":{"resource_types":["routing_policy","quota"],"actors":["user:alice@example.com"]}}'
```
Marco: Good shape. Server should return job id immediately and stream a signed S3 URL when ready. audit-bot: Export job created (id: job-20251031-7a9f).
audit-bot: Job job-20251031-7a9f status=queued, scope=org-12345, requested_by=Alice. ETA ~ 3m.
Priya: For the console preview we can fetch a single event + diff via a lightweight endpoint: /audit/events/{id}?preview=true which returns rendered diff html + raw JSON. Requires the same RBAC checks.
Jon: UX note — in the preview show diffs collapsed by default, and allow 'show full before/after' which hits the signed blob link. Keep page load fast.
Ava: One more ask from legal: export manifests must include hash of exported file + export policy id + operator approval field for long-term retention.
Marco: We can include manifest.json alongside exports with fields: job_id, sha256, policy_version, redaction_profile, operator. That solves chain-of-custody.
Priya: Action items: Marco to prototype precompute-diff pipeline and storage model. Jon to wire up Console preview mock. Ava to capture legal manifest requirements. I'll map retention tiers with infra.
Ava: Thanks all — ping here when prototype exists. :eyes:
